cases.description: 200 application/json with a valid bound card accepts.
A utf-8 charset parameter is accepted.
Charset comparison is case-insensitive.
A quoted utf-8 charset is accepted.
Optional whitespace around the media type and params is tolerated.
A Content-Length within the cap accepts.
A non-numeric Content-Length is ignored, not fatal.
A non-200 2xx status rejects; discovery is a fixed 200 GET.
204 No Content rejects.
A redirect status rejects.
404 rejects.
500 rejects.
An absent Content-Type rejects.
An empty Content-Type rejects.
text/plain rejects.
text/html rejects.
application/ld+json rejects; only application/json is accepted.
application/octet-stream rejects.
A combined or duplicated Content-Type (comma) rejects as ambiguous.
A non-utf-8 charset rejects.
A Content-Length over the 64 KiB cap rejects before the body is trusted.
A Content-Length larger than a 64-bit integer still classifies as over the cap (digit-string comparison, no parse).
An astronomically large Content-Length rejects.
A body whose actual UTF-8 size exceeds the 64 KiB cap rejects.
A multibyte body over the cap rejects; the cap is UTF-8 bytes, not code units, identically in both implementations.
A non-JSON body rejects.
Well-formed JSON that is not an Agent Card rejects.
A JSON array body rejects.
A valid card whose agentId differs from the requested id rejects.
A DID-mediated fetch whose card names a different ownerDid rejects; a host that legitimately publishes a card for one DID must not answer resolution of another with it.
A DID-mediated fetch whose card names the DID under resolution accepts; the comparison is byte for byte with no canonicalization.
The step 9 comparison performs no case folding, so a re-cased ownerDid is a different DID and rejects.
A card without an ownerDid passes step 9 unchanged, even under a DID-mediated fetch.
A fetch that was not DID-mediated passes step 9 unchanged, even when the card carries an ownerDid.
